Heavy-tailed covariates: the t scenario

This note adds one factor to the paper grid of Sivula et al. (2025): the distribution of the covariates. In the paper the covariates are standard normal. Here they are also standard t, with degrees of freedom from 30 down to 1 (Cauchy). Everything else stays as in the paper: the gaussian family, the measure elpd, and the cells of Fig. 5 and Fig. 6.

Render it from the pipeline folder:

Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("notes/xdf_scenario.Rmd", output_dir = ".")'

Data generating process

make_data_gaussian() in workflow/scripts/lib/dgp.R draws one data set of \(n\) observations as

\[ y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_{i1} + \beta_t x_{i2} + \varepsilon_i, \qquad \varepsilon_i \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu_i, \sigma^2), \qquad \beta = (0, 1, \beta_t), \quad \sigma^2 = 1. \]

Model A omits \(x_{2}\). Model B includes it. Both are normal linear regressions with the exact LOO predictive. The quantity of interest is the elpd difference \(\mathrm{elpd}_A - \mathrm{elpd}_B\).

Covariates

The covariates \(x_{ij}\) are independent. With \(\nu\) = x_df they are

\[ x_{ij} = \frac{z_{ij}}{\sqrt{w_{ij} / \nu}}, \qquad z_{ij} \sim \mathrm{N}(0, 1), \qquad w_{ij} = F^{-1}_{\chi^2_\nu}(u_{ij}), \quad u_{ij} \sim \mathrm{U}(0, 1), \]

so \(x_{ij} \sim t_\nu\). For \(\nu = \infty\) the denominator is 1, and \(x_{ij} = z_{ij}\) is the normal covariate of the paper.

  • The t is not rescaled to unit variance. Its variance is \(\nu / (\nu - 2)\), which is infinite for \(\nu \le 2\).
  • \(z\) and \(\varepsilon\) are drawn first, as in the paper. \(u\) is drawn last, and only for a finite \(\nu\). So the normal cells keep the random numbers of the paper run.
  • All t cells share the same \(z\), \(\varepsilon\) and \(u\). Two cells that differ only in \(\nu\) differ only in the tails of the covariates. This gives common random numbers across \(\nu\).

Density of the covariate, linear and log scale.

Outlier

As in the paper, the first observation gets the mean shift

\[ \mu_1 = \Delta \sqrt{\sigma^2 + \lVert \beta \rVert^2}, \qquad \mu_i = 0 \text{ for } i > 1, \]

with \(\Delta\) = out_dev. The scale \(\sqrt{\sigma^2 + \lVert\beta\rVert^2}\) is the SD of \(y\) for a normal covariate. It is kept for the t covariate, so the outlier has the same size in every cell.

Test sets

The test sets come from the same DGP as the training sets, with the same \(\nu\). The target is the elpd difference on 4000 pooled test sets of size \(n\).

Simulation scenarios

Factor Levels
n 32, 128, 512
beta_t 0, 0.2, 1
out_dev 0, 20
x_df 1, 3, 10, 30, Inf (normal)
  • The full product of the factors gives 90 cells. 72 of them have a t covariate.
  • Each cell has 2000 trials (training sets).
  • A t cell has the name of its normal cell plus _t<df>, for example n32_b0_o0_t1.

The figures for the normal covariate keep their names, {fig}_gaussian_elpd.pdf. The figures for a t covariate are {fig}_gaussian_elpd_t<df>.pdf. Each figure shows one \(\nu\).

Results

Each section shows one paper figure. Each tab shows one covariate distribution, from the normal to the Cauchy.
